name: Bicykľáreň
tagline: Bike rental brand drawn in one continuous line.
role: Logo Design, Content Creation, Art Director, PX, UX/UI Designer, Web Designer
outcome: Launched as a sub-brand of Tilia Resort, with online booking that guests mention in their reviews.
about:
Tilia Resort asked me to create Bicykľáreň, a bike rental under its own brand, and I took it from naming and logo to art direction, the website and the booking system. It became my biggest freelance project so far. I kept the resort's colours and typeface, so the rental still feels like part of the resort, and gave it a voice of its own.

Almost every bike rental logo around the lakes of Orava shows a wheel, a gear or a bike, so I drew the ride instead. The wordmark is written in one continuous line, like a route you ride from start to finish, and every illustration follows the same rule. To keep it clear for visitors, the descriptor Bicykľáreň – Bike Rental works as a secondary lockup.

Before I designed the booking, I worked out how the rental runs on the ground: who hands out the bikes, at what time and what can go wrong. I designed and built the website with a reservation system that takes guests from choosing a bike and dates to a confirmed booking, and one review mentions easy ordering with the QR code.

name: maturuj.com
tagline: Exam prep app, from idea to running business.
outcome: Live and bootstrapped, running as a working business.
about:
maturuj.com started as a final school project with an unusual brief: build something worth keeping after graduation, a real product we could sell. Together with Adam Demian I went through the whole cycle, from the first idea and planning to development, testing and launch.

The app prepares students for the Slovak school-leaving exam with personalised AI feedback. It holds digitised exam papers in Slovak language and literature and in English, exercises on the topics students struggle with most, and an assistant that explains why an answer is right instead of only marking it wrong. Most students know the problem well, because they drown in endless notes while the school system moves slowly, so the exam becomes something to survive.

I led the design side: the brand, logo and tone of voice, the UX/UI of the app and the sales materials.

name: Slovensko.sk eDesk
tagline: UX redesign of a national government service.
outcome: Shipped inside a national service used by millions, which keeps being optimised.
about:
eDesk is where Slovak citizens and companies receive and handle official documents from the state. Once the platform became mandatory, every rough edge in it turned into a problem for millions of people at once.

Together with Lighting Beetle we ran the redesign as an ongoing programme instead of a single handover, with stakeholder workshops, feedback from real users and prototypes that we put in front of people and reworked. One design system kept the service consistent while it kept changing.

A large share of the work went into how the service behaves on different screens. People open official mail on a phone while queuing as often as on a desktop at work, so every view had to hold up from a narrow phone to a wide monitor, with the same actions within reach and nothing pushed out of sight or left to horizontal scrolling.

I joined the UX side as a junior designer and worked on the redesign inside that process. It was the first time I saw a service of this scale up close, where one unclear label or a step in the wrong place costs thousands of people an afternoon. A lot of how I work now comes from here, with research first and decisions I can defend.

name: Wezeo Rebrand
tagline: Rebrand clarifying what the team stands for.
role: Logo Design, Content Creation, Art Director
outcome: Adopted as the team’s working brand system across design and communication.
about:
Together with Dávid Drímal I led the rebrand of Wezeo. Working through the whole brand, we came up with the slogan "build different", and later the team changed it to "beyond technology" because it fit what Wezeo does better.

We shaped the messaging, the visual direction and an internal brand system, so the brand describes how Wezeo designs, works together and grows as a team. Today it's the system the team uses across its design and communication.

name: Pro podnikavé Redesign
outcome: 40% increase in returning users after the mobile-first redesign.
about:
Together with Richard Egyed I led the design direction for the Pro podnikavé platform and app redesign. It used to be a slow, web-only experience, and small entrepreneurs needed a mobile-first tool that fits how they actually work.

I focused on the information architecture, simpler navigation and the core flows, so people can find key resources quickly on web and mobile. With the product and development teams we defined a design system and interaction patterns that work the same across devices, and returning users grew by 40% after the redesign.

name: Stelin Home
tagline: Holiday home brand run by a border collie.
outcome: Around 340 Instagram followers without paid ads, and guests who arrive with their dogs.
about:
The owner of a small cabin in Oravská Poruba didn't want his own face on the brand, so he offered his dog's. Her name is Stela, she's a border collie, and today she's officially the owner of Stelin Home.

A dog on the logo tells people the place is pet friendly before they read a word, which speaks straight to the guests most likely to book it. I built the character from Stela's real face, with her own markings and a calm, friendly expression, and set her in olive green, cream and dark wood tones that match the cabin.

The website has its own booking system, so guests can book directly instead of through a big platform, and Stela has her own story there. For Instagram I made templates that the owner fills with his own photos and posts himself.

name: Cabana coffee & bakery
tagline: Café identity built to scale into a bakery.
outcome: Delivered in 24 hours; the logo now runs across all their communication.
about:
A café that was about to expand into a bakery needed an identity that could grow with it, and we had 24 hours to deliver the whole thing.

The new logo is now the core of their brand and runs across all their communication, and both the client and their customers responded well to the fresh direction.

name: AACarabiner
tagline: AAC's first product, prototype to shelf.
outcome: Shipped as a finished product and sold to the community at AAC events.
about:
AACarabiner is the first physical product of Artistic Area Club, designed together with Ján Šefárik. The club lived online, and we wanted something people could carry, an object for people into underground culture who still expect style and function from what they use.

We shaped it as a carabiner 3D-printed from nylon, with an organic silhouette taken from AAC's visual language. Then came a long loop of prototyping, where we printed a version, handed it to people and came back weeks later to ask what held up, what got in the way and what they stopped using. Every round changed the geometry until it carried keys the way it should and survived everyday wear.

What started as an internal experiment is now on sale, and like everything the club makes, its name starts with AAC.

name: Artistic Area Club
tagline: Identity for a creative collective of artists.
role: Logo, Visual Identity, Web, Poster Design, Content Creation
outcome: Grew into a live event series with its own product line, a public archive and over 100K reach.
about:
Music, design and art here mostly ran in separate lanes, and the events that did exist rarely treated any of them with much care. Artistic Area Club started to put them in one room and take the result seriously, and it had to stay open, so the brand could not read like a members-only badge. The logo works from that idea: separate liquids poured together until they set into a single shape, the letters AAC running into one another instead of lining up.

The name is three words long, which is a lot for someone who sees a poster for two seconds, so we hid the short version inside everything the club makes, from AAConcert and AACompetition to AACommunity and AACarabiner. Over time people started calling us simply AAC.

The website carries the same intent. It is a timeline and a portfolio of everything the club has done, so someone arriving cold can see there is real history behind it, and someone who missed a night can see what they missed and show up to the next one. Photos from each event are there to download, so the evening goes home with the people who were in it.

The visual changes from event to event on purpose. One manual applied to everything would turn the club into a company, and the look belongs to the artists who build each night. A few elements repeat; the rest is made once and stays tied to that one evening.

name: Logofolio
tagline: Logos shaped around different brand identities.
about: A selection of logos I designed for different clients between 2023 and 2025, each one shaped around that brand's own identity and needs.

name: Posterfolio
tagline: Posters for a range of clients and events.
about: Posters I designed for different clients and events between 2023 and 2026, each one built around the theme of its own event.

name: ÆRv Cover Series
tagline: Playlist covers that show how AAC sounds.
about:
ÆRv is a playlist for the vibe the AAC brand stands for. We wanted people to know roughly how AAC sounds, so we put together a playlist they could put on and listen to.

I designed the covers in a dark style, with a custom ÆRv logotype as the main symbol, and the series also includes a vinyl design, so every piece looks like it belongs together.

name: Oravská knižnica
tagline: Digital and print design for a public library.
about:
I took care of digital communication and visual content for the public library in Dolný Kubín. Most of the work was social media posts announcing events for the local community.

I also designed posters and diplomas and prepared materials for print, all in line with the library's visual identity.
